candidates.source:
NAME = "cascade-2"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # Two-step expected gain: seeding u tips each out-neighbour v with prob
    # P1-P0; if v tips, next round v itself drives activations worth r_v.
    P0 = prob(f.a)
    P1 = prob(f.a + 1)
    D = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)       # marginal activation per target
    r = D @ graph.adjT                            # prob-mass each target would tip next round
    gain = (D * (1.0 + r)) @ graph.adjT           # depth-1 tip + that tip's depth-2 spread
    gain = gain + f.eligible * (1.0 - P0)         # the seed itself (kept non-zero for ties)
    return gain

candidates.name: llm-tip-front
candidates.source:
NAME = "tip-front"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # Gate-style priority derived from prob (works for any g, and for graded
    # laws), plus hub spread and the cascade term gate-g never credits:
    # flipping a node is worth more if that node has live out-neighbours.
    P0 = prob(f.a)
    P1 = prob(f.a + 1)
    D = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)
    r = D @ graph.adjT
    cross = f.eligible & (P0 < 0.5) & (P1 >= 0.5)  # one push likely completes the gate
    W = D + 2.0 * cross.astype(float) * (1.0 + r)  # strong bonus for crossable gates that cascade
    gain = W @ graph.adjT + f.eligible * (1.0 - P0)
    return gain

candidates.source:
NAME = "cascade-3"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # Depth-three lookahead: value of tipping v grows with the spread it and
    # its downstream tips can generate; capped so deep fanout doesn't blow up.
    P0 = prob(f.a)
    P1 = prob(f.a + 1)
    D = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)
    r = np.minimum(D @ graph.adjT, 6.0)
    gain = (D * (1.0 + r + 0.4 * r * r)) @ graph.adjT
    gain = gain + f.eligible * (1.0 - P0)
    return gain

candidates.name: llm-gate-cross
candidates.source:
NAME = "gate-cross"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # Like gate-2, but the gate position is read off prob() instead of hard-coding a==1:
    # a node is "completing" if one more active in-neighbour crosses its activation
    # threshold, "progressing" otherwise. Keyed to H0 (lt) where thresholds vary per node,
    # so gate-2's fixed a==1 cut mis-targets nodes with other gate positions.
    P0 = prob(f.a)
    P1 = prob(f.a + 1)
    comp = f.eligible & (P1 >= 0.5) & (P0 < 0.5)
    prog = f.eligible & (P1 < 0.5)
    score = (comp.astype(float) + 0.3 * prog.astype(float)) @ graph.adjT
    return score + 1e-3 * f.eligible

candidates.name: llm-tiered-gate
candidates.source:
NAME = "tiered-gate"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # Tiered build-up: weight each out-neighbour v by how many seeded pushes it still
    # needs to cross its threshold (read from prob, not assumed). Completing nodes
    # (dist 1) get full weight; nodes 2, 3, 4 pushes away get geometrically decayed
    # progress weight 0.6^(d-2); nodes never reaching 0.5 get a floor so they are
    # still preferred over dead picks when nothing else is available.
    dist = np.full(f.a.shape, 99.0)
    for i in range(5):
        hit = f.eligible & (prob(f.a + i) >= 0.5) & (dist > 90)
        dist = np.where(hit, float(i), dist)
    w = np.where(
        dist < 1e-8, 0.0,
        np.where(dist < 1.5, 1.0,
                 np.where(dist < 90, 0.6 ** np.maximum(dist - 2.0, 0.0), 0.05)),
    )
    return w @ graph.adjT + 1e-3 * f.eligible

candidates.name: llm-cascade-2
candidates.source:
NAME = "cascade-2"   # two-step expected gain: hub + discounted next-round spread

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # Hub gets the immediate round exactly right; it ignores that any node we
    # newly activate this round survives as an active in-neighbour next round
    # and fires its own out-neighbours.  Add that second-order term.
    P0 = prob(f.a)
    P1 = prob(f.a + 1.0)
    q = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)          # marginal activation per target
    g0 = q @ graph.adjT + f.eligible * (1.0 - P0)   # hub's one-round gain
    T = q @ graph.adjT                              # future spread if the target fires now
    g1 = (q * T) @ graph.adjT                       # value of activating each out-neighbour
    return g0 + 0.6 * g1 + 1e-3 * f.eligible

candidates.name: llm-domino-2
candidates.source:
NAME = "domino-2"   # hard-gate cascade: only gate-completing hits, + chain value

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # For (near-)deterministic threshold laws, soft marginals blur the targeting:
    # only out-neighbours that flip from below-threshold to at-threshold matter.
    # Weight those fully, and bonus candidates whose completed gates can
    # complete further gates next round (domino chains).
    P0 = prob(f.a)
    P1 = prob(f.a + 1.0)
    flip = f.eligible & (P0 < 0.5) & (P1 >= 0.5)
    q = flip.astype(float)
    g0 = q @ graph.adjT + f.eligible * (1.0 - P0)
    T = q @ graph.adjT                     # gates this node's firing would complete
    g1 = (q * T) @ graph.adjT              # chain potential of the candidate
    return g0 + 0.7 * g1 + 1e-3 * f.eligible

candidates.name: llm-expose-2
candidates.source:
NAME = "expose-2"   # memory-aware: spread now + invest exposure in near-threshold nodes

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # Infer each node's threshold from prob (no hard-coded law parameters):
    # theta_hat = a + #{t >= 1 : prob(a + t) < 0.5}.
    th = f.a + np.zeros_like(f.a)
    for t in range(1, 6):
        th = th + (prob(f.a + float(t)) < 0.5).astype(float)
    # Exposure gap under the current cumulative-exposure estimate f.E.
    gap = th - f.E
    # need1: one more exposure fires it (now or remembered); need2: two more.
    need1 = (f.eligible & (gap > 1e-9) & (gap <= 1.0)).astype(float)
    need2 = (f.eligible & (gap > 1.0) & (gap <= 2.0)).astype(float)
    P0 = prob(f.a)
    P1 = prob(f.a + 1.0)
    q = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)          # immediate marginal (non-memory part)
    spread = (q + 0.85 * need1 + 0.5 * need2) @ graph.adjT
    # Under memory laws an exposure persists, so seeding nodes that are 1-2
    # short -- even if they cannot fire this round -- is worth almost as much
    # as an immediate activation; under non-memory laws E == a and the extra
    # terms coincide with the gate hits hub already counts.
    return spread + f.eligible * (1.0 - P0) + 1e-3 * f.eligible

NAME = "cascade-2"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    P0 = prob(f.a)
    P1 = prob(f.a + 1)
    D = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)      # marginal activation of each target
    fut = D @ graph.adjT                        # expected spread of each target if it fires this round
    w = D * (1.0 + fut)                         # value of triggering v now + its next-round reach
    return w @ graph.adjT + f.eligible * (1.0 - P0) + 1e-3 * f.eligible

candidates.name: llm-memory-push
candidates.source:
NAME = "memory-push"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    P0 = prob(f.a)
    P1 = prob(f.a + 1)
    D = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)
    mem = (np.abs(f.E - f.a).sum(axis=-1) > 1e-9).astype(float)   # law carries exposure
    unclosed = (1.0 - P1) * (f.a + 1 >= 1)                        # absorbs exposure, stays inactive
    w = D + 0.6 * mem[:, None] * unclosed
    return w @ graph.adjT + f.eligible * (1.0 - P0) + 1e-3 * f.eligible

candidates.name: llm-chain-gate
candidates.source:
NAME = "chain-gate"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    P0 = prob(f.a)
    P1 = prob(f.a + 1)
    comp = (P0 < 0.5) & (P1 >= 0.5)             # one seed completes the gate
    prog = (P1 < 0.5) & (f.a + 1 >= 1)          # receives exposure, still below gate
    C = np.where(f.eligible, comp.astype(float) + 0.3 * prog.astype(float), 0.0)
    fut = C @ graph.adjT                        # completions this node will unlock if it fires
    w = C * (1.0 + fut)
    return w @ graph.adjT + f.eligible * (1.0 - P0) + 1e-3 * f.eligible
